items.name: UST Mon 16 Nov (intraday, Asia/Europe session): 10y ~5.13-5.15% holding near one-month high, 2y 4.85%, 30y 5.46%; Dec 25bp hike 92% priced
items.headline: US 10-Year Yield Holds Near One-Month High (tradingeconomics, 16 Nov)
items.claim: The 10-year yield hovered around 5.15% on Monday (TE quote 5.13%, -1bp), close to one-month highs, with the 2y at 4.85% and 30y at 5.46%, as markets price a 92% chance of a 25bp Fed hike in December after hot October inflation and hawkish Fed comments, with some policymakers floating 50bp; focus on Warsh remarks and the October FOMC minutes Wednesday. Friday 13 Nov TE close was 5.15-5.16% after a ~30bp weekly rise.
items.source: tradingeconomics US 10Y page and 16 Nov news note; Saxo Asia Market Quick Take 16 Nov
items.note: Intraday Monday levels, NOT a close. TE Friday 13 Nov print (5.15-5.16%) is 3-4bp above the 5.12% press level recorded 11-13; source difference, not a new move. Saxo: 2y rose as much as 37bp last week; RBC sees back-to-back Dec/Jan hikes; Man Group's Rowe sees 10y 5.5% early 2027. No stress signal beyond level - market is consolidating, not extending.

items.name: Gilts Mon 16 Nov (intraday): 10y 5.35% highest since 23 Oct, 2y 5.00% three-year high, 30y 5.78%; Dec BoE hike ~80%, two more by Jun-27
items.headline: UK Gilt Yields Surge as Rate Hike Expectations Mount (tradingeconomics, 16 Nov)
items.claim: UK 10-year yields rose above 5.35% on Monday, the highest since 23 October, and two-year yields passed 5% to a three-year high as investors priced further BoE hikes after this month's first hike since 2023; markets see ~80% odds of a December hike with two more expected by June 2027, ahead of Wednesday's October CPI (consensus 3.6%, one-year high).
items.source: tradingeconomics UK 10Y page and 16 Nov news note; Saxo Asia Quick Take 16 Nov (CPI expectation)
items.note: TE prints 10y 5.35% (+1bp), 2y 5.00% (+1.7bp), 30y 5.78% (-0.4bp). The 11-13 file recorded gilt 10y 5.478% from another source - TE's series is ~13bp lower; treat the two as different quote sources, not a 13bp Monday rally. Au79 (14 Nov) had 30y 5.82% Friday, consistent with TE's 5.78% Monday. Rate-driven, not credit stress.

items.name: JGB Mon 16 Nov (intraday): 10y 2.89% (+3bp, near three-week high), 30y 4.04%, 40y 4.18% despite Q3 GDP -0.1% annualised; USD/JPY 159.82, Katayama warns on 'one-sided, rapid moves'
items.headline: Japan 10Y Yield Steady Despite Weak GDP Data (tradingeconomics) / Asia Market Quick Take 16 Nov (Saxo)
items.claim: The JGB 10y held near 2.87-2.89% on Monday, close to three-week highs, even as Q3 GDP unexpectedly contracted 0.1% annualised (exp +0.1%, Q2 +1.7%); 30y 4.04% and 40y 4.18% (both +3bp); markets still expect further BoJ tightening (policy rate 1.25%, Summary of Opinions broadly supportive of hikes, December hike expected) and JGBs tracked the US selloff. USD/JPY ~159.82 near 160 with FinMin Katayama warning against one-sided rapid moves; no intervention reported.
items.source: tradingeconomics Japan 10Y page and 16 Nov note; Saxo Asia Market Quick Take 16 Nov
items.note: Intraday, not a close. Extends the 11-13 JGB hit (10y 2.86%, 30y 4.01% record, 40y 4.16%) by ~3bp across the curve. Bloomberg 16 Nov 'Investors return to JGBs as rate outlook shifts, SMBC Nikko says' surfaced but refused host - not fetched; headline suggests dip-buying, not stress. Mizuho +6.5% on guidance raise (Saxo).

items.name: Bloomberg 16 Nov: Indonesia faces uphill battle to stem rupiah slide - Fri close 18,195/USD, -9% YTD (worst since 2022), BI intervening in spot/NDF/secondary bonds, BI decision Wed 18 Nov, $5.6bn MSCI-exit outflow risk
items.headline: Indonesia faces uphill battle to stem rupiah's slide (Bloomberg via Free Malaysia Today, 16 Nov 08:48 MYT)
items.claim: The rupiah closed Friday at 18,195 per dollar, down about 9% year-to-date and heading for its worst year since 2022; Bank Indonesia is intervening in the spot market, offshore and onshore NDFs and buying government bonds in the secondary market; BI meets Wednesday 18 Nov with a slim majority expecting no change (Macro Hive: even a 25bp hike 'would probably not be enough'); foreigners have sold $5.6bn of Indonesian stocks this year and Goldman estimates a further $5.6bn passive outflow if Indonesia is removed from MSCI indices; BNP sees 18,500 by end-2027, MUFG 18,350 this quarter.
items.note: Follow-on to the 11-12 record-low 18,241-18,253 / BI intervention hit; Friday close 18,195 is a modest recovery from the record low. No bond yield level or intervention amount in the article. Vietnam dollar bond: no new development surfaced since the 11-12 'on hold' item.

items.name: Philippines BTr partially awards Mon 16 Nov T-bills: P42.3bn of P45bn, 364-day capped at P7.5bn; 91d 6.567% (+7.4bp), 182d 6.748% (+2.9bp), 364d 6.932% (+7.7bp); tenders P67.5bn vs P85.1bn prior week
items.headline: T-bill yields climb as rate hike prospects persist (Context.ph) / BTr partially awards T-bills as yields rise further (BusinessWorld)
items.claim: The Bureau of the Treasury raised P42.3bn against a P45bn programme on 16 Nov, fully awarding the 91- and 182-day bills but partially awarding the 364-day bill (capped at P7.5bn) as average yields rose to 6.567%, 6.748% and 6.932% respectively on persistent consumer price pressures and expectations of further BSP tightening; total tenders fell to P67.5bn from P85.1bn a week earlier.
items.note: Partial award = issuer rejecting high bids, not a failed auction (still 1.5x covered). bp changes are computed from the printed averages. Same day BusinessWorld reports PSEi at a six-year low on economic worries. Not US Treasury - recorded because the sweep surfaced it as the only in-gate auction with a stress claim.

items.name: Bloomberg 16 Nov: $488m Malaysia data-center loan (Epoch Digital / Actis) syndication delayed as arranging banks seek more lenders - 'rare deal pause'
items.headline: Asian Data Center Loan Syndication Is Delayed in Rare Deal Pause (Bloomberg) / $488M Loan for Malaysian Data Center Project Delayed During Syndication
items.claim: Syndication of a $488m loan backing an Actis-backed Epoch Digital data-center project in Malaysia has been delayed while being marketed to other lenders: the arranging banks want more participants, original bank-meeting and site-visit dates were missed (executives unavailable) and new dates are being scheduled; Bloomberg describes it as a rare pause in Asian data-center financing.
items.source: Bloomberg via huggingnews relay (16 Nov 04:41 EST); The Edge Singapore and FourWeekMBA relays client_error; Bloomberg refused host
items.sweep_query: 6. gigawatt deferral data center (DCD variant) / 1. bond deal pulled OR downsized
items.note: Delayed, not pulled or downsized; no lenders named; FourWeekMBA headline links the project to ByteDance (not confirmed in the relay read). Small ($488m) and non-hyperscaler - a tell on bank appetite for DC project debt in Asia, not a hard event.

items.name: Australian bank credit widens 16 Nov: Westpac A$2.5bn senior priced 9-10bp wider than CBA/ANZ mid-year 66-67bp/swap; NAB A$3.25bn incl. Tier 2 at 158bp, >=30bp wider than Feb/Aug comps
items.headline: Credit Spreads Widen (16 November 2026) - Fixed Income News Australia
items.claim: Westpac raised A$2.5bn of senior unsecured paper 9-10bp wider than the 66-67bp over swap CBA (July) and ANZ (August) paid, placing 44% of the FRNs with Asian investors; NAB raised A$3.25bn across three tranches with its Tier 2 subordinated notes at 158bp over swap, at least 30bp wider than comparable 10NC5 deals from CBA (February) and Westpac (August), amid the RBA hike and choppy global markets; Franklin Templeton's Sonal Desai expects two to three more US hikes.
items.candidate_dial: D-credit (bank spreads, not a pulled deal)
items.source: Fixed Income News Australia, published 2026-11-16 10:33 AEDT
items.note: Deals completed, not pulled; recorded as a dated spread-widening observation. Implied Westpac senior ~75-77bp/swap is arithmetic, not printed. ASIC updated private-credit standards 'last week' (undated).

items.name: Bloomberg 15 Nov: US IG spread 86bp Fri (-5bp w/w), IG yields ~6% highest since GFC; 'tech companies slowing their bond sales'; banks plan ~$21bn high-grade in 2027 for $63bn Broadcom/Anthropic chip package; Ruffer doubled duration
items.headline: US corporate bonds attract investors as stock market turbulence grows (Bloomberg / Davide Barbuscia, via Business Standard 15 Nov)
items.claim: IG spreads averaged 86bp on Friday 13 Nov, slightly wider than the year's mean but tight by two-decade standards and 5bp tighter on the week, while IG yields averaged ~6%, near the highest since the financial crisis (from ~4.8% at the start of the year); high-grade issuance is up 28% YTD and on track for a record (BofA ~$2.1trn 2026, ~$1.9trn 2027) but tech companies are slowing their bond sales; banks plan up to ~$21bn of high-grade bonds next year within a $63bn Broadcom funding package for Anthropic chips (L&G's Woodside: chip financing into 2027 'can weigh on credit a bit'); Ruffer doubled portfolio duration since July as a hedge against an AI-buildout slowdown.
items.sweep_query: 1. bond deal pulled OR downsized (postponed/market conditions variant)
items.note: No pulled or postponed deals reported; benign credit read (spreads tightening, demand strong). The $63bn Broadcom/Anthropic package and ~$21bn bank bonds are forward 2027 supply, relevant to issuance group. Weekend wrap carrying in-gate (Fri close) spread fact.

items.name: Nscale S-1/A (filed 12 Nov): 'must obtain additional financing to meet forecast obligations in 2027' (Sept filing said funded 12 months); ~$1.7bn 9m net loss on $307m revenue, ~$5.5bn debt end-Sep, $44.6bn Anthropic contract, ~$35bn IPO target
items.headline: Nscale warns it needs more cash ahead of $35bn IPO (FT via Dealroom 13 Nov) / Nscale plc Form S-1/A filed 2026-11-12
items.claim: In Amendment No.1 to its S-1 filed 12 Nov, Nvidia-backed neocloud Nscale said it must obtain additional financing to meet forecast obligations in 2027 after ordering Vera Rubin GPUs for its up-to-$44.6bn Anthropic services agreements (dated 25 Aug 2026) at the Monarch campus, reversing September's statement that it was funded for at least 12 months; estimated nine-month net loss ~$1.7bn on $307m revenue, debt ~$5.5bn at end-September, with >$5.7bn project financings, a $900m revolver and ~$4.9bn GPU financings disclosed; IPO price range still blank.
items.candidate_dial: D-credit (neocloud funding stress; not a repricing)
items.source: SEC S-1/A Nscale plc 2026-11-12 (first 100k chars read; 2027 language per FT via Dealroom 13 Nov); Axios 13 Nov and Benzinga surfaced (Benzinga client_error)
items.sweep_query: 4. funding round repriced AI lab (neocloud variant)
items.note: Dated 12 Nov, not in dedupe_events.txt (the 11-05 Nscale item there is Microsoft walking away from Loughton) - kept once with late:true. Not a repricing or pulled deal: a going-concern-style funding warning from a neocloud with a $44.6bn anchor contract, one week before the Anthropic IPO. The 2027 sentence was not located in the first 100k chars of the 1.4m-char filing; it is carried from FT/Dealroom. Six-month revenue in filing $140.6m (vs $10.4m prior year).
